|  |  |
|  |  |
|  | def\_over\_trunk(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, scale: float) -\> tuple\[Tensor, Tensor\]: |
|  | """Every branch token over all of the trunk, with its log-sum-exp. Each KV |
|  | head's query group is folded into the query axis, so the trunk's keys are |
|  | read once and never repeated.""" |
|  | batch, heads, length, dim = q.shape |
|  | kv = k.shape\[1\] |
|  | ifnot \_fused(q): |
|  | return \_cat(\[\_explicit(part, k, v, None, scale) for part in q.split(CHUNK, dim=2)\]) |
|  | folded = q.reshape(batch, kv, heads // kv \* length, dim) |
|  | out, lse = torch.ops.aten.\_scaled\_dot\_product\_flash\_attention(folded, k, v, 0.0, False, False, scale=scale)\[:2\] |
|  | return out.reshape(batch, heads, length, dim).float(), lse.reshape(batch, heads, length) |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  | def\_own(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, tree: Tree, window: int \| None, scale: float) -\> tuple\[Tensor, Tensor\]: |
|  | """Each branch over its own tokens, causally (within \`window\`), with its log-sum-exp.""" |
|  | ifnot \_fused(q) andlen(tree.branch) <= CHUNK: \# small enough for one masked product |
|  | same, off = tree.branch\[:, None\] == tree.branch\[None\], tree.offset |
|  | allowed = same & (off\[None\] <= off\[:, None\]) |
|  | if window isnotNone: |
|  | allowed &= off\[None\] \> off\[:, None\] \- window |
|  | return \_explicit(q, k, v, allowed, scale) |
|  | ifnot \_fused(q): \# branch by branch: memory grows with the longest question, not with the batch |
|  | parts = \[\] |
|  | for a, b inzip(tree.cu\[:-1\].tolist(), tree.cu\[1:\].tolist()): |
|  | off = torch.arange(b - a, device=q.device) |
|  | allowed = off\[None\] <= off\[:, None\] |
|  | if window isnotNone: |
|  | allowed &= off\[None\] \> off\[:, None\] \- window |
|  | parts.append(\_explicit(q\[:, :, a:b\], k\[:, :, a:b\], v\[:, :, a:b\], allowed, scale)) |
|  | return \_cat(parts) |
|  | local = {} if window isNoneelse {"window\_size\_left": window - 1, "window\_size\_right": 0} |
|  | out, lse = torch.ops.aten.\_flash\_attention\_forward( |
|  | \*(t\[0\].transpose(0, 1) for t in (q, k, v)), tree.cu, tree.cu, tree.longest, tree.longest, |
|  | 0.0, True, False, scale=scale, \*\*local)\[:2\] |
|  | return out.transpose(0, 1)\[None\].float(), lse\[None\] |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  | def\_merge(a: tuple\[Tensor, Tensor\], b: tuple\[Tensor, Tensor\]) -\> Tensor: |
|  | (oa, la), (ob, lb) = a, b |
|  | m = torch.maximum(la, lb) |
|  | wa, wb = (la - m).exp(), (lb - m).exp() |
|  | return (oa \* wa\[..., None\] \+ ob \* wb\[..., None\]) / (wa + wb)\[..., None\] |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  | def\_windowed(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, window: int, scale: float) -\> Tensor: |
|  | """Causal attention within \`window\`, as local blocks: each block of \`window\` |
|  | queries sees its own block and the one before it.""" |
|  | batch, heads, length, dim = q.shape |
|  | blocks = -(-length // window) |
|  |  |
|  | defsplit(t: Tensor) -\> Tensor: \# (B, H, T, D) -> (B, blocks, H, window, D) |
|  | t = F.pad(t, (0, 0, 0, blocks \* window - length)) |
|  | return t.reshape(batch, t.shape\[1\], blocks, window, dim).transpose(1, 2) |
|  |  |
|  | defwith\_previous(t: Tensor) -\> Tensor: |
|  | return torch.cat((F.pad(t, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))\[:, :-1\], t), dim=3) |
|  |  |
|  | qb, kb, vb = split(q), with\_previous(split(k)), with\_previous(split(v)) |
|  | qpos = torch.arange(window, device=q.device)\[:, None\] \+ window |
|  | kpos = torch.arange(2 \\* window, device=q.device)\[None, :\] |
|  | allowed = (kpos <= qpos) & (kpos > qpos - window) |
|  | first = allowed & (kpos >= window) \# block 0 has no block before it |
|  | mask = torch.stack(\[first\] + \[allowed\] \* (blocks - 1))\[:, None\].repeat(batch, 1, 1, 1) |
|  | out = F.scaled\_dot\_product\_attention(qb.flatten(0, 1), kb.flatten(0, 1), vb.flatten(0, 1), |
|  | attn\_mask=mask, scale=scale, enable\_gqa=True) |
|  | out = out.reshape(batch, blocks, heads, window, dim).transpose(1, 2) |
|  | return out.reshape(batch, heads, blocks \* window, dim)\[:, :, :length\] |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  | defcausal\_attention(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, window: int \| None, scale: float) -\> Tensor: |
|  | """Right-padded chains: causal, within \`window\` if set.""" |
|  | if window isNoneor q.shape\[2\] <= window: |
|  | return F.scaled\_dot\_product\_attention(q, k, v, is\_causal=True, scale=scale, enable\_gqa=True) |
|  | return \_windowed(q, k, v, window, scale) |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  | defattention(q: Tensor, k: Tensor, v: Tensor, tree: Tree \| None, window: int \| None, scale: float) -\> Tensor: |
|  | """Chains, or a tree: the trunk causally, each branch over the trunk and over |
|  | its own tokens.""" |
|  | if tree isNone: |
|  | return causal\_attention(q, k, v, window, scale) |
|  | p = tree.p |
|  | qb = q\[:, :, p:\] |
|  | mine = \_own(qb, k\[:, :, p:\], v\[:, :, p:\], tree, window, scale) |
|  | if p == 0: |
|  | return mine\[0\].to(q.dtype) |
|  | trunk = causal\_attention(q\[:, :, :p\], k\[:, :, :p\], v\[:, :, :p\], window, scale) |
|  | if window isNone: |
|  | seen = \_over\_trunk(qb, k\[:, :, :p\], v\[:, :, :p\], scale) |
|  | else: \# only the trunk's last window-1 keys are in reach of a branch |
|  | tail = min(p, window - 1) |
|  | allowed = torch.arange(p - tail, p, device=q.device)\[None\] \> tree.positions\[p:, None\] \- window |
|  | seen = \_explicit(qb, k\[:, :, p - tail:p\], v\[:, :, p - tail:p\], allowed, scale) |
|  | return torch.cat((trunk, \_merge(seen, mine).to(q.dtype)), dim=2) |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  | \# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # |
|  | \# the stack |
|  | \# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  | classDecoderLayer(GradientCheckpointingLayer): |
|  | """Norm, operator (\`conv\` or \`self\_attn\`), residual; norm, MLP, residual. |
|  | \`sandwich\` adds a norm on each branch's output.""" |
|  |  |
|  | def\_\_init\_\_(self, kind: str, operator: nn.Module, mlp: nn.Module, dim: int, eps: float, sandwich: bool): |
|  | super().\_\_init\_\_() |
|  | self.operator\_name = "conv"if kind == "conv"else"self\_attn" |
|  | setattr(self, self.operator\_name, operator) |
|  | self.feed\_forward = mlp |
|  | self.operator\_norm = RMSNorm(dim, eps) |
|  | self.ffn\_norm = RMSNorm(dim, eps) |
|  | self.post\_operator\_norm = RMSNorm(dim, eps) if sandwich else nn.Identity() |
|  | self.post\_ffn\_norm = RMSNorm(dim, eps) if sandwich else nn.Identity() |
|  |  |
|  | defforward(self, x: Tensor, pos: Tensor, tree: Tree \| None = None) -\> Tensor: |
|  | h = x + self.post\_operator\_norm(getattr(self, self.operator\_name)(self.operator\_norm(x), pos, tree)) |
|  | return h + self.post\_ffn\_norm(self.feed\_forward(self.ffn\_norm(h))) |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  | classLanguageModel(nn.Module): |
|  | """Embedding, the hybrid stack and the final norm, called like HF's text models. |
|  |  |
|  | Rows are right-padded, so the causal operators never let a pad reach a real |
|  | token and there is no attention mask to apply. |
|  | """ |
|  |  |
|  | def\_\_init\_\_(self, cfg, operator: Callable\[\[str\], nn.Module\], mlp: Callable\[\[\], nn.Module\], |
|  | eps: float, sandwich: bool = False): |
|  | super().\_\_init\_\_() |
|  | self.embed\_tokens = nn.Embedding(cfg.vocab\_size, cfg.hidden\_size) |
|  | self.layers = nn.ModuleList( |
|  | DecoderLayer(kind, operator(kind), mlp(), cfg.hidden\_size, eps, sandwich) for kind in cfg.layer\_types) |
|  | self.embedding\_norm = RMSNorm(cfg.hidden\_size, eps) \# the final norm, despite its name |
|  |  |
|  | defget\_input\_embeddings(self) -\> nn.Embedding: |
|  | return self.embed\_tokens |
|  |  |
|  | defrun(self, h: Tensor, tree: Tree \| None = None) -\> Tensor: |
|  | pos = tree.positions if tree isnotNoneelse torch.arange(h.shape\[1\], device=h.device) |
|  | for layer in self.layers: |
|  | h = layer(h, pos, tree) |
|  | return self.embedding\_norm(h) |
|  |  |
|  | defforward(self, input\_ids=None, inputs\_embeds=None, \*\*\_) -\> BaseModelOutputWithPast: |
|  | h = self.embed\_tokens(input\_ids) if inputs\_embeds isNoneelse inputs\_embeds |
|  | return BaseModelOutputWithPast(last\_hidden\_state=self.run(h)) |
|  |  |
|  | defanswer(self, trunk: Tensor, questions: Tensor, lengths: Tensor) -\> Tensor: |
|  | """Final hidden states at the last token of every question, in one pass. |
|  | \`trunk\` \`(1, P, d)\` embeddings; \`questions\` the ids of all questions back |
|  | to back, \`(sum(lengths),)\`.""" |
|  | tree = Tree(trunk.shape\[1\], lengths) |
|  | h = self.run(torch.cat((trunk, self.embed\_tokens(questions)\[None\]), dim=1), tree) |
|  | return h\[0, tree.leaves\] |
|  |  |

|  | """LFM2-VL and LFM2 on the hybrid stack. |
|  |  |
|  | HF's classes stay the frame (the SigLIP2 tower, the projector, the image |

|  | module names, so checkpoints load and save unchanged. A state with any number |
|  | of questions runs as one \`hybrid.Tree\`, with the same outputs as HF's own |
|  | implementation. |

|  | from \_\_future\_\_ import annotations |
|  |  |
|  | import torch |
|  | import torch.nn as nn |
|  | import torch.nn.functional as F |
|  | from transformers import Lfm2Config, Lfm2VlConfig |
|  | from transformers.models.lfm2.modeling\_lfm2 import Lfm2ForCausalLM as HfLfm2 |
|  | from transformers.models.lfm2\_vl.modeling\_lfm2\_vl import Lfm2VlForConditionalGeneration as HfLfm2Vl |
|  |  |
|  | from .hybrid import LanguageModel, RMSNorm, Tree, attention, causal\_conv, rope |
|  |  |
|  |  |
|  | classAttention(nn.Module): |
|  | """GQA with per-head q/k norms and RoPE over the whole head.""" |
|  |  |
|  | def\_\_init\_\_(self, cfg): |
|  | super().\_\_init\_\_() |
|  | self.heads, self.kv\_heads = cfg.num\_attention\_heads, cfg.num\_key\_value\_heads |
|  | self.head\_dim = getattr(cfg, "head\_dim", None) or cfg.hidden\_size // self.heads |
|  | self.q\_proj = nn.Linear(cfg.hidden\_size, self.heads \* self.head\_dim, bias=False) |
|  | self.k\_proj = nn.Linear(cfg.hidden\_size, self.kv\_heads \* self.head\_dim, bias=False) |
|  | self.v\_proj = nn.Linear(cfg.hidden\_size, self.kv\_heads \* self.head\_dim, bias=False) |
|  | self.out\_proj = nn.Linear(self.heads \* self.head\_dim, cfg.hidden\_size, bias=False) |
|  | self.q\_layernorm = RMSNorm(self.head\_dim, cfg.norm\_eps) |
|  | self.k\_layernorm = RMSNorm(self.head\_dim, cfg.norm\_eps) |
|  | self.theta = cfg.rope\_parameters\["rope\_theta"\] |
|  | self.scale = self.head\_dim\*\*-0.5 |
|  |  |
|  | defforward(self, x: torch.Tensor, pos: torch.Tensor, tree: Tree \| None) -\> torch.Tensor: |
|  | batch, length, \_ = x.shape |
|  | q = self.q\_layernorm(self.q\_proj(x).view(batch, length, self.heads, self.head\_dim)) |
|  | k = self.k\_layernorm(self.k\_proj(x).view(batch, length, self.kv\_heads, self.head\_dim)) |
|  | v = self.v\_proj(x).view(batch, length, self.kv\_heads, self.head\_dim) |

|  | super().\_\_init\_\_() |

|  | if cfg.block\_auto\_adjust\_ff\_dim: \# HF's sizing rule, kept exactly |

|  | if cfg.block\_ffn\_dim\_multiplier isnotNone: |

|  | self.w3 = nn.Linear(cfg.hidden\_size, hidden, bias=False) |

|  |  |
|  |  |

|  | """HF's LFM2 with the hybrid language model, under HF's name.""" |
|  |  |

"""Synthetic CPU-only feasibility check; never reads journal or user data."""
import json
import resource
import statistics
import time
from pathlib import Path

import torch
from transformers import AutoModel

torch.set_num_threads(4)
torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)
started = time.perf_counter()
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
    str(Path.home() / "mrmr-d1-candidate/checkpoint"),
    trust_remote_code=True, local_files_only=True, dtype=torch.float32,
).eval()
print(json.dumps({"load_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started}), flush=True)
questions = {
    "category": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which category best describes this system service event?", "criteria": {
        "incident": "A service is broken, unavailable, repeatedly failing, or losing data now.",
        "noise": "Routine startup, shutdown, retry, or warning chatter needing no attention.",
        "FYI": "Useful operational information that is neither an incident nor routine noise.",
    }},
    "requires_action": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the operator genuinely need to take action?"},
    "severity": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How severe is the operational impact?", "criteria": ["No impact", "Degraded with workaround", "Unavailable or data at risk"]},
}
for name, state, qs in [
    ("one", "The service has failed repeatedly and is unavailable.", {"category": questions["category"]}),
    ("three", "The service has failed repeatedly and is unavailable.", questions),
    ("long", "Routine heartbeat: the service is healthy. " * 400 + "Now the disk is full and all writes fail.", questions),
]:
    times = []
    for _ in range(4):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        result = model.system_one(state, qs)
        times.append(time.perf_counter() - start)
    print(json.dumps({"workload": name, "cold_seconds": times[0], "warm_median_seconds": statistics.median(times[1:]), "warm_seconds": times[1:], "usage": result["usage"], "answers": result["answers"], "peak_rss_kib": resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss}), flush=True)

"""Offline HTTP boundary checks; no Torch, weights, credentials, or network service."""

import copy
import http.client
import json
import threading
import unittest

from serve import DecisionServer, MAX_BODY, model_id


class ServingTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_http_contract_and_rejection(self):
        # Own and join the server thread even on assertion failure. The fake
        # only supplies inference; serialization/auth/validation use real HTTP.
        calls = []
        fail = False
        identity = model_id()
        token = "synthetic-test-token-not-a-secret-1234"

        def decide(state, questions):
            if fail:
                raise RuntimeError("private model state must not escape")
            calls.append((state, questions))
            return {
                "answers": {
                    "category": {"type": "choice", "choice": "incident", "confidence": 0.9,
                                 "probabilities": {"incident": 0.9, "noise": 0.1}},
                    "action": {"type": "noul", "noul": 0.8},
                    "severity": {"type": "score", "score": 0.8, "confidence": 0.8,
                                 "probabilities": {"0": 0.2, "1": 0.8},
                                 "legend": {"0": "Low", "1": "High"}},
                },
                "usage": {"input_tokens": 100, "output_tokens": 0},
            }

        server = DecisionServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), decide, token, identity)
        worker = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever)
        worker.start()

        def request(body, auth=token, path="/v1/systemone", method="POST", extra=None):
            conn = http.client.HTTPConnection(*server.server_address, timeout=3)
            try:
                headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + auth, "Content-Type": "application/json"}
                headers.update(extra or {})
                conn.request(method, path, body, headers)
                response = conn.getresponse()
                return response.status, json.loads(response.read())
            finally:
                conn.close()

        valid = {
            "model": identity,
            "state": {"data": {"message": "Synthetic incident", "id": 9007199254740993}},
            "questions": {
                "category": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Classify", "criteria": {"incident": "Broken", "noise": "Routine"}},
                "action": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Act?", "criteria": {"true": "Yes", "false": "No"}},
                "severity": {"type": "score", "instructions": "Severity?", "criteria": ["Low", "High"]},
            },
        }
        try:
            status, result = request(json.dumps(valid))
            self.assertEqual(status, 200)
            self.assertEqual(result["model"], identity)
            self.assertEqual(result["usage"]["output_tokens"], 0)
            self.assertEqual(calls[0][0]["data"]["id"], 9007199254740993)
            self.assertEqual(set(result["answers"]), set(valid["questions"]))
            self.assertEqual(request(None, path="/health", method="GET")[0], 200)
            self.assertEqual(request("{}", auth="wrong")[0], 401)
            self.assertEqual(request("{}", path="/chat/completions")[0], 404)
            self.assertEqual(request("x" * (MAX_BODY + 1))[0], 413)
            self.assertEqual(request("{}", extra={"Content-Type": "text/plain"})[0], 415)
            self.assertEqual(request("{}", extra={"Transfer-Encoding": "chunked"})[0], 400)
            for raw in ["{", "[]", "{}", '{"state": 1, "state": 2}',
                        json.dumps(valid).replace('"Synthetic incident"', "NaN"),
                        json.dumps(valid).replace('"Synthetic incident"', "1e999")]:
                self.assertEqual(request(raw)[0], 400)
            for patch in [
                {"model": model_id(True)}, {"images": ["http://never-fetch.invalid"]},
                {"questions": {}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "unknown", "instructions": "?"}}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "noul", "instructions": ""}}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "?", "criteria": {"true": "Yes"}}}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "score", "instructions": "?", "criteria": ["One"]}}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "?", "criteria": {"a.b": "A", "b": "B"}}}},
                {"questions": {"x": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "?", "criteria": {"a": 1, "b": "B"}}}},
            ]:
                value = copy.deepcopy(valid)
                value.update(patch)
                self.assertEqual(request(json.dumps(value))[0], 400)
            self.assertEqual(len(calls), 1, "invalid requests must never reach inference")
            fail = True
            status, result = request(json.dumps(valid))
            self.assertEqual(status, 500)
            self.assertNotIn("private", json.dumps(result))
        finally:
            server.shutdown()
            worker.join(timeout=3)
            server.server_close()
            self.assertFalse(worker.is_alive())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Bounded synthetic timings through the same decider used by the HTTP server.

Not a quality evaluation. Never substitutes for labeled real events. Load and
warm timings are separate, and Linux peak RSS includes model loading/conversion.
"""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import resource
import statistics
import time

from serve import load_decider, model_id


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--int8", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    started = time.perf_counter()
    decide = load_decider(args.checkpoint.resolve(), 4, args.int8)
    print(json.dumps({"model": model_id(args.int8), "load_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started}), flush=True)
    questions = {
        "category": {"type": "choice", "instructions": "Which category best describes this system service event?", "criteria": {
            "incident": "A service is broken, unavailable, repeatedly failing, or losing data now.",
            "noise": "Routine startup, shutdown, retry, or warning chatter needing no attention.",
            "FYI": "Useful operational information that is neither an incident nor routine noise.",
        }},
        "requires_action": {"type": "noul", "instructions": "Does the operator genuinely need to take action?"},
        "severity": {"type": "score", "instructions": "How severe is the operational impact?", "criteria": ["No impact", "Degraded with workaround", "Unavailable or data at risk"]},
    }
    short = "The service has failed repeatedly and is unavailable."
    for name, state, qs in [
        ("one", short, {"category": questions["category"]}),
        ("three", short, questions),
        ("longer", "Routine heartbeat: the service is healthy. " * 20 + "Now the disk is full and all writes fail.", questions),
    ]:
        times = []
        for _ in range(4):
            start = time.perf_counter()
            result = decide(state, qs)
            times.append(time.perf_counter() - start)
        assert result["usage"]["output_tokens"] == 0
        assert set(result["answers"]) == set(qs)
        print(json.dumps({
            "workload": name, "cold_seconds": times[0],
            "warm_median_seconds": statistics.median(times[1:]), "warm_seconds": times[1:],
            "usage": result["usage"], "answers": result["answers"],
            "peak_rss_kib": resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss,
        }, allow_nan=False), flush=True)
    # Ensure an over-limit request fails before spending inference, not after
    # the runtime's HTTP timeout. This checks the real pinned tokenizer path.
    try:
        decide("heartbeat " * 2000, questions)
    except ValueError:
        print('{"over_limit_rejected": true}', flush=True)
    else:
        raise AssertionError("token ceiling was not enforced")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Opt-in real-model integration check. Owns all processes and uses only synthetic data.

Run under the resource-limited scope in README.md. No service is installed, no
source starts, and the temporary database/configuration are removed on exit.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import secrets
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

import yaml

from serve import model_id


def stop(process):
    if process is not None and process.poll() is None:
        process.terminate()
        try:
            process.wait(timeout=15)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            process.kill()
            process.wait()


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--binary", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--int8", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    recipe = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    binary = str(args.binary.resolve())
    env = dict(os.environ, MRMR_D1_API_KEY=secrets.token_hex(32))
    # Never stop an existing listener to make a test work. Both processes will
    # also fail binding if another process wins the small check/start race.
    for port in (8091, 4242):
        with socket.socket() as sock:
            sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))
    # Ignore HTTP proxy environment variables: synthetic local traffic and the
    # bearer token must never be sent through a configured external proxy.
    http = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))

    def request(url, body=None, auth=False):
        headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
        if auth:
            headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + env["MRMR_D1_API_KEY"]
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None, headers=headers)
        with http.open(req, timeout=180) as response:
            return json.load(response)

    def ready(process, port, model=False):
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 90
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if process.poll() is not None:
                raise RuntimeError("owned process exited before ready")
            try:
                if model:
                    health = request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/health", auth=True)
                    assert health["model"] == model_id(args.int8)
                else:
                    with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=1):
                        pass
                return
            except (OSError, urllib.error.URLError):
                time.sleep(0.2)
        raise RuntimeError("owned process did not become ready")

    model_process = runtime_process = None
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="mrmr-d1-smoke-") as tmp:
        # Logs contain only synthetic events. Keep them private and temporary;
        # never copy live journal data into this verification harness.
        os.chmod(tmp, 0o700)
        with open(Path(tmp) / "process.log", "w") as log:
            try:
                command = [sys.executable, str(recipe / "serve.py"), "--checkpoint", str(args.checkpoint.resolve())]
                if args.int8:
                    command.append("--int8")
                model_process = subprocess.Popen(command, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=log)
                ready(model_process, 8091, model=True)
                cfg = yaml.safe_load((recipe / "mrmr.example.yaml").read_text())
                cfg["models"]["d1"]["model"] = model_id(args.int8)
                cfg["db"]["path"] = str(Path(tmp) / "smoke.db")
                # Force only the synthetic smoke through a shadow notification.
                # This checks the successful pipeline, not classification quality.
                cfg["policy"] = []
                cfg["default"] = {"notify": {"via": "stdout"}, "shadow": True}
                config = str(Path(tmp) / "mrmr.yaml")
                Path(config).write_text(yaml.safe_dump(cfg))

                def start_runtime():
                    process = subprocess.Popen([binary, "run", "-config", config], env=env, stdout=log, stderr=log)
                    # The caller owns cleanup even if readiness fails.
                    return process

                runtime_process = start_runtime()
                ready(runtime_process, 4242)
                event = {
                    "type": "setup.test", "source": "d1-smoke", "subject": "synthetic-service",
                    "data": {"message": "Synthetic incident: the fictional service is unavailable and all writes fail."},
                    "metadata": {"source_event_id": "synthetic-1"},
                }
                started = time.perf_counter()
                result = request("http://127.0.0.1:4242/api/events", event)
                elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
                assert result["decision"]["status"] == "ok", "model response was not accepted"
                assert result["decision"]["model"] == model_id(args.int8)
                assert result["outcome"] == "notify"

                def inspect():
                    return json.loads(subprocess.check_output([binary, "inspect", result["event_id"], "-config", config], env=env, stderr=log))

                stored = inspect()
                assert len(stored["decisions"]) == len(stored["executions"]) == 1
                assert stored["executions"][0]["status"] == "shadow"
                assert stored["trace"]
                assert request("http://127.0.0.1:4242/api/events", event)["duplicate"]
                stop(runtime_process)
                runtime_process = start_runtime()
                ready(runtime_process, 4242)
                assert request("http://127.0.0.1:4242/api/events", event)["duplicate"]
                assert len(inspect()["decisions"]) == 1
                print(json.dumps({"model": model_id(args.int8), "pipeline_seconds": elapsed,
                                  "decision": "ok", "execution": "shadow", "persisted_trace": True,
                                  "dedup_before_and_after_restart": True}), flush=True)
            finally:
                stop(runtime_process)
                stop(model_process)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Temporary synthetic comparison driver, with owned inference subprocess."""
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import secrets
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
import yaml

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path("recipe").resolve()))
from serve import model_id
from smoke import stop

env = dict(os.environ, MRMR_D1_API_KEY=secrets.token_hex(32))
config = yaml.safe_load(Path("recipe/mrmr.example.yaml").read_text())
config["models"]["d1"]["model"] = model_id(True)
Path("eval-int8.yaml").write_text(yaml.safe_dump(config))
http = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))
with open("eval-server.log", "w") as log:
    server = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "recipe/serve.py", "--checkpoint", "checkpoint", "--int8"], env=env, stdout=log, stderr=log)
    try:
        deadline = time.monotonic() + 90
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            if server.poll() is not None:
                raise RuntimeError("server exited")
            try:
                req = urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:8091/health", headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + env["MRMR_D1_API_KEY"]})
                with http.open(req, timeout=3) as response:
                    assert json.load(response)["model"] == model_id(True)
                break
            except OSError:
                time.sleep(0.2)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError("server did not become ready")
        print(json.dumps({"ready_rss": [x for x in Path(f"/proc/{server.pid}/status").read_text().splitlines() if x.startswith("VmRSS:")][0]}), flush=True)
        started = time.perf_counter()
        with open("eval-int8-progress.log", "w") as progress, open("eval-int8.json", "w") as result:
            subprocess.run(["./mrmr", "eval", "-config", "eval-int8.yaml", "-dataset", "generated-eval.jsonl"], env=env, stdout=result, stderr=progress, check=True, timeout=300)
        print(json.dumps({"eval_seconds": time.perf_counter() - started}), flush=True)
        print(Path("eval-int8.json").read_text(), flush=True)
    finally:
        stop(server)

arguments.content:
# Local d1 / System One candidate

Run LiquidAI's pinned d1-3B on a CPU behind mrmr's **existing** System One
HTTP contract. This recipe does not add a provider, change the default model,
start sources, enable effects, or install a background service.

**Status: integration verified on Marvin; NOT promoted.** See [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md).
Full precision works but is slow. Experimental int8 is faster, changes judgments,
and missed too many notifications under the provisional policy. Neither variant
has passed the required 50+ labeled **real-event** gate.

## Boundary

```text
mrmr → POST /v1/systemone → local d1 → typed answers → mrmr validation/policy
```

`provider: typesafe` is the existing protocol selector, not a hosted-provider
requirement. The configured `base_url` determines the destination; this recipe
uses loopback. Other compatible servers can later use the same client. Merely
serving d1 through `/chat/completions` does not implement this decision interface.

The adapter adds the loaded model identity to d1's native `answers`/`usage`
response. It does not invent summaries, change probabilities, select outcomes,
fetch state URLs, or accept image/file inputs. `confidence` in this pinned d1
implementation is the largest option probability, not a separate certainty score.

Model identities include the revision **and precision variant**. The client must
request the exact loaded identity. No automatic model selection or cloud fallback.

## Prepare a fresh candidate

Requirements: Linux x86_64, Python 3.11 with venv, adequate RAM, and a built mrmr
binary. The recorded CPU dependency lock is not a promise of support on every
platform. Do not modify the system Python or an existing model environment.

From the repository root, choose an unused user-owned directory:

```sh
umask 077
work="$HOME/mrmr-d1-candidate"
mkdir "$work"                       # fails rather than overwriting a candidate
mkdir "$work/recipe"
cp recipes/local-d1/* "$work/recipe/"
python3.11 -m venv "$work/.venv"
"$work/.venv/bin/pip" install -r "$work/recipe/requirements.lock"
"$work/.venv/bin/pip" check

HF_HUB_DISABLE_IMPLICIT_TOKEN=1 "$work/.venv/bin/hf" download LiquidAI/d1-3B \
  --revision da1fe36a861f24690f27f622dca1d8688503d113 \
  --local-dir "$work/checkpoint"
```

The checkpoint is approximately 6.25 GB. It contains executable Python loaded via
`trust_remote_code=True`: review `api.py`, `modeling_d1.py`, `prompt.py`, `runner.py`,
`lfm2_vl.py`, and `hybrid.py` before running. Keep the checkpoint directory at the
pinned revision; don't replace its contents while retaining the old model ID.
Serving loads only local files in Hub offline mode, including the tokenizer.

Weights use the [LFM Open License](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/d1-3B/blob/main/LICENSE),
with a $10M annual-revenue commercial-use restriction, not an unrestricted
Apache/MIT license. No weights or upstream model code are bundled in mrmr.

## Run temporarily, with limits

On Marvin, first inspect available memory and Plex/Hermes/existing inference
activity. The initial fp32 load (also required before int8 conversion) peaked at
about **17.8 GiB RSS**. Do not run both variants simultaneously. Leave room for
other services; the 20 GiB cap below is specific to the measured 30 GiB host.

```sh
export MRMR_D1_API_KEY="$(python3 -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))')"
cd "$work"
systemd-run --user --scope --unit=mrmr-d1-candidate \
  -p MemoryHigh=18G -p MemoryMax=20G -p MemorySwapMax=0 -p CPUQuota=400% \
  nice -n 10 timeout --kill-after=10 900 \
  .venv/bin/python recipe/serve.py --checkpoint checkpoint
```

This is a foreground, 15-minute candidate, **not** an enabled service. Ctrl-C
stops it. From another terminal, `systemctl --user stop mrmr-d1-candidate.scope`
stops the owned scope. A fresh start takes several seconds; int8 conversion adds
roughly 25 seconds. Never use a restart loop to conceal memory or model failures.

Supply the **same** `MRMR_D1_API_KEY` to mrmr's environment without printing it or
putting it in YAML. Authentication is required even on loopback. For persistent
operation, provision it via an approved secret mechanism after deployment review.

Copy `mrmr.example.yaml` into your candidate directory and set an absolute,
private database path. Start a built mrmr binary with that file:

```sh
/path/to/mrmr run -config "$work/mrmr.yaml"
```

All configured notifications are shadowed. No journal/poller is enabled. Source
allowlists and real-event data access need separate review before activation.

For the experimental int8 variant, add `--int8` to the serving command and change
the model ID suffix in YAML from `:cpu-fp32` to `:cpu-int8-channel`. This quantizes
only the language model's linear layers, per channel, retaining an fp32 output
head. It is **not** numerically equivalent to fp32 or a vendor-calibrated quant.
The PyTorch quantization API is deprecated; the tested version is pinned. Do not
upgrade it without repeating numerical checks and evaluation.

## Serving limits

- Loopback IPv4 only, default port 8091. Use an SSH tunnel if needed; review any
  non-loopback deployment separately. Stdlib HTTP serving is not an internet edge.
- `GET /health` requires the same bearer token and reports the loaded model ID.
- `POST /v1/systemone`: exact `model`, `state`, `questions`; no other fields.
- At most 16 KiB JSON, 8 questions, and 1,024 **summed full-question prompt tokens**.
  The token sum deliberately overcounts shared state. Oversized input is rejected,
  never silently truncated; mrmr records failure and ignores it.
- One request at a time, small listen backlog, five-second socket I/O timeout.
  This is not a throughput server. A client timeout does not cancel native Torch
  work; the process-level resource/time limits above remain important.
- No request/response logging, raw model error echo, execution tools, or policy.
  mrmr still validates every returned probability and result field.

## Checks

Offline HTTP/auth/validation check, no Torch or weights required:

```sh
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s recipes/local-d1 -v
```

After installing the checkpoint, run these **one at a time** under the same
resource-limited scope as above (replace the `serve.py` command):

```sh
.venv/bin/python recipe/benchmark.py --checkpoint checkpoint
.venv/bin/python recipe/benchmark.py --checkpoint checkpoint --int8
.venv/bin/python recipe/smoke.py --checkpoint checkpoint --binary /path/to/mrmr
.venv/bin/python recipe/smoke.py --checkpoint checkpoint --binary /path/to/mrmr --int8
```

The benchmark emits synthetic cold/warm timings, probabilities, Linux peak RSS,
and a token-ceiling check. It is not an accuracy benchmark. `smoke.py` owns and
stops its model/runtime processes, checks SQLite trace + shadow execution and
deduplication across restart, then removes its temporary synthetic database.
It refuses occupied ports; no other service is stopped.

For the repository's generated-data comparison, with the chosen server running
and a matching model variant in the candidate configuration:

```sh
/path/to/mrmr eval -config "$work/mrmr.yaml" -dataset testdata/generated-eval.jsonl
```

For a Jev comparison, copy that config and change only the model connection to
`base_url: https://api.typesafe.ai/v1`, `api_key_env: TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, and
`model: jev-1.13.0`. Hosted evaluation sends event content to TypeSafe; the recorded
comparison used **only generated synthetic fixtures**, not journal/email data.
Use identical questions/policy and record validation failures separately from
judgment errors. Score thresholds need per-model calibration, not blind copying.

## Promotion remains a human decision

Collect at least 50 representative, labeled real events with approved source
access. Measure missed notifications, false alerts, validity, latency, and host
contention. Include adversarial/noisy inputs. Test the exact precision variant;
quantized probabilities cannot inherit full-precision thresholds.

Agree acceptance thresholds before tuning. Do not tune to this generated set and
call it a real-event gate. Keep effects shadowed and the global default unchanged
until reviewed. Persistent service installation, network exposure, and source
activation are also separate approval steps.

# Marvin candidate results

These are feasibility and integration results, **not a promotion decision**.
No real journal/email data was read or sent to a hosted model. No default was
changed, no sources were enabled, and no persistent service was installed.

## Environment

- Marvin: Intel Core Ultra 9 185H, AVX2, 22 logical CPUs, approximately 30 GiB RAM.
- Before testing: about 26 GiB available, existing inference idle; Plex,
  `lfm25.service`, and the Hermes user service active.
- Isolated Python 3.11 environment; Torch 2.14.1+cpu, Transformers 5.19.0.
  Full dependency versions are in `requirements.lock`.
- `LiquidAI/d1-3B`, revision `da1fe36a861f24690f27f622dca1d8688503d113`.
- Four Torch intra-op threads, one inter-op thread, nice 10, CPUQuota 400%,
  MemoryHigh 18 GiB, MemoryMax 20 GiB, MemorySwapMax 0. Sequential tests only.
- No CPU affinity or competing-load stress test. Availability checks are not
  proof that Plex playback or Hermes responsiveness was unaffected under load.

## Feasibility

Initial unquantized CPU test, warm medians over three runs:

| Workload | Input tokens reported | fp32 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| One question, short synthetic incident | 85 | 6.41 s |
| Three questions, same incident | 148 | 11.12 s |

The initial longer-state test (400 repeated heartbeat sentences) did not finish
its four-run workload before the overall 600-second process limit. There is no
per-request long-input latency result from that run. This prompted an explicit,
conservative CPU token ceiling in the serving recipe.

Naive whole-model dynamic int8 was faster, but changed `requires_action.noul`
from **0.819 to 0.402** on the same three-question synthetic incident. Rejected
as a serving variant; its preliminary script is retained only in the private
candidate directory for audit.

The shipped **experimental** variant uses per-channel dynamic quantization of
language-model linear layers and leaves the output head in fp32. The same Noul
became **0.761**, still not equivalent to fp32. Final `benchmark.py --int8` run:

| Workload | Input tokens reported | Warm median (three runs) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| One question | 85 | 0.555 s |
| Three questions | 148 | 1.015 s |
| Three questions, 20 heartbeat sentences + failure | 329 | 2.072 s |

- Load + conversion: 27.5 s in that run.
- Peak RSS, including initial full-precision loading: about 17.8 GiB for both
  variants. Int8 ready-state RSS in the evaluation run: about 6.7 GiB.
- Over-limit input rejected before inference using the pinned tokenizer.
- Small samples, not tail-latency guarantees or comparisons against GPU claims.

## Real-model integration

`smoke.py` passed on Marvin for **both** variants using the unchanged Go client:

- Authenticated local System One request with Choice, Noul, and Score.
- Validated Decision with pinned precision-specific model identity.
- Persisted Event, Decision, execution, and trace in SQLite.
- Notification recorded as `shadow`, not executed.
- Duplicate suppressed before and after restarting mrmr; still one Decision.
- Owned processes stopped and temporary synthetic database removed.

Single synthetic end-to-end event: **21.70 s fp32**, **1.89 s int8-channel**.
These are pipeline measurements, not directly comparable to the shorter
benchmark prompts above. fp32 remains the recipe default; int8 is explicit opt-in.

## Generated-set comparison

Same 50 cases from `testdata/generated-eval.jsonl`, same questions and provisional
policy from this recipe, with only the model connection changed. Both category
confidence and action probability gates were `>= 0.85`. This is a measurement of
**model + validation + untuned policy**, not a pure model accuracy leaderboard.

| Metric | d1 CPU int8-channel | Jev 1.13.0 (hosted) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Valid decisions | 50/50 | 40/50 |
| Category correct | 30/50 | 33/50 |
| Requires-action correct (Noul >= 0.5) | 48/50 | 40/50 |
| Outcome correct | 36/50 | 36/50 |
| False ignores among expected notifications | **14/18** | **11/18** |

The d1 run took 89.2 seconds excluding server startup. All expected-ignore cases
routed to ignore, but that is little comfort when most expected notifications
were also ignored. Several correct category/action judgments were suppressed
by the untuned 0.85 gates; category errors also occurred, including `smoke-alarm`
classified as noise. No thresholds were tuned against these fixtures.

Jev's ten invalid decisions confound a quality comparison: nine Score answers
failed the current probability-weighted consistency check (reported differences
at the 0.01 rounding boundary), and one Choice disagreed with its highest reported
probability. Validation was **not weakened** to force the comparison through.
The rounding-boundary handling needs separate investigation and a regression
check before repeating the comparison. Invalid outputs correctly failed to ignore.

The full fp32 checkpoint has **not** been run across this 50-case set. Do not
attribute quantized quality results to the full-precision checkpoint.

## Remaining gates / retained artifacts

The candidate on Marvin is under `~/mrmr-d1-candidate/`: isolated environment,
pinned checkpoint, serving recipe, Linux mrmr binary, and synthetic timing/eval
logs. The smoke tokens were ephemeral process environment values, not written
into configuration. Processes are stopped; no autostart unit was installed.

Before promotion:

1. Investigate Jev's response-consistency failures separately; repeat the baseline.
2. Collect 50+ representative labeled **real** events with approved data access.
3. Compare exact model variants, tune on separate data, and agree acceptable
   false-ignore/false-alert rates before enabling effects.
4. Measure latency/headroom while Marvin's actual workloads are active.
5. Review source activation and any persistent deployment independently.

Keep the project default unchanged. The reusable System One integration works;
the judgment quality and deployment economics have not earned promotion yet.

why run int8?

Because full-precision inference on Marvin took **~22 seconds per event**. I tried int8 as a CPU optimization; it brought that down to **~1.9 seconds**.

But **quantization changes the model’s judgments**, not just its speed. We observed that directly.

I let the performance experiment get ahead of the quality baseline. **We should have run the full-precision model through the same 50-event evaluation first.** The int8 results don’t establish whether the original d1 is good enough.

Full precision remains the candidate configuration; int8 is opt-in. Next should be the unmodified model’s evaluation—not more quantization tuning.
_damn_ that's rough. maybe marvin itself isn't the best machine to run _inference_ on. and just runs the mrmr service and inference is run somewhere else?

**Yes. Marvin is a good runtime host; that doesn’t make it the right inference host.** We conflated those two roles.

```text
Marvin: events → SQLite → filters
                            ↓
                  System One endpoint
                  on an inference machine
                            ↓
Marvin: validated decision → policy → outcome
```

That preserves everything important:
- **Authority and durable state stay on Marvin.**
- Events can stay within your private network—still local-first, not necessarily same-machine.
- The inference backend is replaceable through the configured endpoint. No core redesign needed.

**My recommendation:** keep mrmr on Marvin and evaluate unquantized d1 on accelerator-backed hardware. Deepthought is the obvious candidate to inspect, but we shouldn’t disrupt its existing model service or assume it has spare capacity.

Then run the same quality evaluation and measure **end-to-end latency including transport**. For ambient events, a small network hop is preferable to forcing CPU inference into an unsuitable performance envelope.

Marvin should be the reference **runtime deployment**, not a requirement that every model execute there.
ok is mrmr set up to have inference run on a different machine?

**Yes—the mrmr client already supports remote inference.** Each model has a configurable `base_url` and optional bearer authentication. Events go over HTTP; validation, policy, and storage stay on Marvin.

**What isn’t configured yet:** the d1 candidate server currently listens only on `127.0.0.1`. To use it remotely, we’d need:
- An SSH tunnel, or an explicitly configured authenticated tailnet listener.
- Marvin’s model `base_url` pointed at that endpoint.

No Go runtime redesign required—just inference-server deployment and connection configuration.

its four-run workload before the overall 600-second process limit. There is no
per-request long-input latency result from that run. This prompted an explicit,
conservative CPU token ceiling in the serving recipe.

Naive whole-model dynamic int8 was faster, but changed `requires_action.noul`
from **0.819 to 0.402** on the same three-question synthetic incident. Rejected
as a serving variant; its preliminary script is retained only in the private
candidate directory for audit.

The shipped **experimental** variant uses per-channel dynamic quantization of
language-model linear layers and leaves the output head in fp32. The same Noul
became **0.761**, still not equivalent to fp32. Final `benchmark.py --int8` run:

| Workload | Input tokens reported | Warm median (three runs) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| One question | 85 | 0.555 s |
| Three questions | 148 | 1.015 s |
| Three questions, 20 heartbeat sentences + failure | 329 | 2.072 s |

- Load + conversion: 27.5 s in that run.
- Peak RSS, including initial full-precision loading: about 17.8 GiB for both
  variants. Int8 ready-state RSS in the evaluation run: about 6.7 GiB.
- Over-limit input rejected before inference using the pinned tokenizer.
- Small samples, not tail-latency guarantees or comparisons against GPU claims.

## Real-model integration

`smoke.py` passed on Marvin for **both** variants using the unchanged Go client:

- Authenticated local System One request with Choice, Noul, and Score.
- Validated Decision with pinned precision-specific model identity.
- Persisted Event, Decision, execution, and trace in SQLite.
- Notification recorded as `shadow`, not executed.
- Duplicate suppressed before and after restarting mrmr; still one Decision.
- Owned processes stopped and temporary synthetic database removed.

Single synthetic end-to-end event: **21.70 s fp32**, **1.89 s int8-channel**.
These are pipeline measurements, not directly comparable to the shorter
benchmark prompts above. fp32 remains the recipe default; int8 is explicit opt-in.

## Generated-set comparison

Same 50 cases from `testdata/generated-eval.jsonl`, same questions and provisional
policy from this recipe, with only the model connection changed. Both category
confidence and action probability gates were `>= 0.85`. This is a measurement of
**model + validation + untuned policy**, not a pure model accuracy leaderboard.

| Metric | d1 CPU int8-channel | Jev 1.13.0 (hosted) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Valid decisions | 50/50 | 40/50 |
| Category correct | 30/50 | 33/50 |
| Requires-action correct (Noul >= 0.5) | 48/50 | 40/50 |
| Outcome correct | 36/50 | 36/50 |
| False ignores among expected notifications | **14/18** | **11/18** |

The d1 run took 89.2 seconds excluding server startup. All expected-ignore cases
routed to ignore, but that is little comfort when most expected notifications
were also ignored. Several correct category/action judgments were suppressed
by the untuned 0.85 gates; category errors also occurred, including `smoke-alarm`
classified as noise. No thresholds were tuned against these fixtures.

Jev's ten invalid decisions confound a quality comparison: nine Score answers
failed the current probability-weighted consistency check (reported differences
at the 0.01 rounding boundary), and one Choice disagreed with its highest reported
probability. Validation was **not weakened** to force the comparison through.
The rounding-boundary handling needs separate investigation and a regression
check before repeating the comparison. Invalid outputs correctly routed to ignore.

The full fp32 checkpoint has **not** been run across this 50-case set. Do not
attribute quantized quality results to the full-precision checkpoint.

## Remaining gates / retained artifacts

The candidate on Marvin is under `~/mrmr-d1-candidate/`: isolated environment,
pinned checkpoint, serving recipe, Linux mrmr binary, and synthetic timing/eval
logs. The smoke tokens were ephemeral process environment values, not written
into configuration. Processes are stopped; no autostart unit was installed.

Before promotion:

1. Investigate Jev's response-consistency failures separately; repeat the baseline.
2. Collect 50+ representative labeled **real** events with approved data access.
3. Compare exact model variants, tune on separate data, and agree acceptable
   false-ignore/false-alert rates before enabling effects.
4. Measure latency/headroom while Marvin's actual workloads are active.
5. Review source activation and any persistent deployment independently.

Keep the project default unchanged. The reusable System One integration works;
the judgment quality and deployment economics have not earned promotion yet.
